ash: Heads-up — Canary CI picked up a p95 decode regression (~+28%) after the fused-op reorder merge (commit abcdef1). infra-ci-bot posted the perf job failure.

infra-ci-bot: [perf-job] build/branch=main - decode_p95: baseline=42ms, current=54ms, alert=threshold_exceeded :robot_face:

kelly: Ugh. Do we have a quick flamegraph/profile?

ash: Pasted the short profiling snapshot below. reproducer run is a small chat workload (seq=96 avg, batch=1/2).
```
# top of flamegraph (sample counts)
fused_attn_kernel_dispatch  3800
kv_prefetch_worker         2900
decode_loop               5200
matmul_dense_fused         4200
# perf stat snippet
cycles: 1.2e9
L1-dcache-loads: 4.3e7
cache-misses: 3.2e6 (miss rate jumped from 4.1% -> 12.6% vs baseline)
```

ash: Also saw kv prefetch miss rate jump in logs: `kv_prefetch: miss_rate=0.43` vs baseline `0.12`. Looks correlated with the fused-op ordering changes.

matt: Can we bisect to the exact commit? My hunch is the kernel ordering change nudged prefetch to run after the first matmul microkernel, which increases the hotset churn.

kelly: If that's true then single-thread warmup & microbatching will be affected. Might only show up on shortseq P95, which is what CI tests.

ash: I started a bisect across the last 8 merges. Early result points to abcdef1 -> modifies fused-op scheduler op order + adds lightweight inline cache for kernel hints.

sara: Can we reproduce locally? Ash, share the exact invocations you used.

ash: Repro steps:
```
git checkout abcdef1
export REDWOOD_DEBUG_KERNEL_SELECTOR=1
./tools/infer_bench --model=redwood/small-test --seq=96 --batch=1 --warmup=50 --steps=200 --log-kv=1
```
Logs show `kernel_hint=matmul_fused_v2` for step 0..10 and then fallback to `matmul_fused_v1` after increase in kv misses.

matt: Can you paste the kernel selector trace?

ash: snippet: `selector: choose(matmul_fused_v2) because latency_est=3.1ms, kv_prefetch_est=0.8ms -> chosen; step 12: kv_prefetch_queue=high -> choose(matmul_fused_v1)`

kelly: So the selector is oscillating mid-run. That explains the variance and p95 tail. The new inline cache probably decays too fast under shortseq access patterns.

matt: Two immediate mitigations: 1) pin kernel hint to the previous ordering in the canary fleet, 2) revert the inline-cache decay tweak. Which is faster?

sara: I'm leaning revert for canary to buy time. I'll open the revert PR now. :eyes:

infra-ci-bot: revert-pr opened: GH#4821 revert abcdef1 -> branch: revert/inline-cache-decay. Running canary rollout hold.

ash: After reverting locally I re-ran the bench — p95 back to 43ms (within noise). kv miss rate back to 0.11.

kelly: Great. Can we confirm prod/canary metrics once the revert lands? If it recovers we can mark rollout-blocker resolved.

sara: Revert merged and canary paused. infra-ci-bot: canary metrics updated — decode_p95 now 44ms. Canary will ramp if stable. :thumbsup:

matt: Post-mortem items:
- Add a microbench that simulates shortseq + single-concurrent requests to catch selector oscillation.
- Add a deterministic replay test for the kernel-inline-cache eviction heuristic.
- Add a new metric to Console: `kernel_selector_flip_rate` per model/route.

ash: Also need to dig into why kv prefetch miss rate amplifies; maybe fused matmul v2 has slightly different memory access pattern that increases KV cache churn when ordering changes. I'll follow up with memtrace.

kelly: Assign owners? ash -> root cause analysis & memtrace, matt -> selector unit tests, sara -> add canary test in CI. I'll create tickets.

ash: temp label: rollout-blocker, priority=high. Thanks everyone.

sara: Nice quick work. Revert + tests should keep us safe while we investigate. :relieved:

matt: FYI I'll run a bisect job across a narrower window to confirm that the inline-cache decay param is the culprit and drop a minimal patch that retains the performance win but avoids oscillation.

ash: I'll drop the memtrace + sample outputs into the bug ticket. linking flamegraphs: https://internal.flame/redwood/173/seq96-fuse-vs-baseline.svg

infra-ci-bot: [note] perf job history: https://ci.internal/reports/branches/main/perf-history

kelly: Thanks — closing this slack thread, moving discussion to GH PR and ticket tracker.
